summary: 1931 L-4 lookout on Dog Mountain's south shoulder, replaced by a second cab in 1953 and removed in 1967; a concrete anchor block remains beside the public trail.

facts.design: Gable-roofed L-4 cab with windows on three sides (1931), replaced by a second L-4 cab (1953)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1967 (dismantled, removed or destroyed, depending on the source). A concrete block that anchored the lookout is the only remains reported.

access.note: The site lies beside the popular Dog Mountain Trail, which starts on the north side of Route 14 at milepost 53.

visit.trail_note: A 6-mile trail from Route 14 at milepost 53 leads to the former site on the south shoulder of the summit.

events.note: Gable-roofed L-4 cab with windows on three sides, built to watch for fires across the river in Oregon.
A Columbia National Forest employee was stationed alone at the lookout when a rattlesnake bit him; he recovered.
Second L-4 cab. Wikipedia gives 1952; a historical report quoted on Washington Lookouts has an entry dated February 8, 1954.
Dismantled (Wikipedia), removed (FFLOS register) or destroyed (firelookout.com, WillhiteWeb).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia gives 1952. The FFLOS register, WillhiteWeb and the blog give 1953. A historical report quoted on Washington Lookouts has an entry dated February 8, 1954. The story uses 1953 and says the sources disagree.
Wikipedia says dismantled, the FFLOS register says removed, and firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. The year agrees across sources; only the word differs.

WillhiteWeb says the mountain was used as a fire lookout point around 1920, and the hiking blog mentions a lookout camp set up before the first cabin. The other sources date the first structure to 1931. The story says a lookout went up in 1931 without calling it the first, and leaves out the 1920 claim.

notes_for_editor: Core dates (1931 build, 1953 replacement, 1967 removal) agree across the FFLOS, WillhiteWeb and Wikipedia pages, but firetower.org, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb share much of the same wording, so they are not independent. The only account of remains is one personal blog. Brief coordinates (45.71268, -121.69905) sit about 0.5 km from the Wikipedia/GNIS Dog Mountain Lookout coordinates (45.717062, -121.701186); worth checking on the FFLOS map. Brief elevation 755.9 m was not checked against a source; WillhiteWeb gives the lookout site as 2,505 feet. No new photos found.
